name: GHK-Cu (copper peptide)

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Cell, rat and rabbit wound studies

track.title: Phase I
track.line: No published Phase I trial found

what.text: GHK-Cu is a chain of three amino acids, glycine, histidine and lysine, bound to a copper ion (glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine-Cu2+). Studies also call it copper tripeptide or tripeptide-copper complex. It is used in skin care products.

src.label: Miller et al., Arch Facial Plast Surg, 2006
Canapp et al., Vet Surg, 2003

what.text: How it acts, according to cell and animal studies

items.text: In human skin cells (fibroblasts) grown in the lab, GHK-Cu made normal and radiation-damaged cells multiply faster. The damaged cells made more of two growth factors, bFGF and VEGF.

src.label: Pollard et al., Arch Facial Plast Surg, 2005

items.text: In rats with poorly supplied skin wounds, a GHK-Cu gel was linked to smaller wounds and lower levels of TNF-alpha and two tissue-breaking enzymes, MMP-2 and MMP-9.

src.label: Canapp et al., Vet Surg, 2003

items.text: In rabbits with open wounds, a GHK-Cu product was linked to smaller unhealed wound areas and faster growth of new tissue than no treatment.

src.label: Cangul et al., Vet Dermatol, 2006

what.text: These effects were seen in cells and animals. They have not been shown in people.

research.text: Human evidence on skin is thin. We found one small randomized study (13 people finished) and one single-patient report that used GHK-Cu mixed with four other ingredients. One Phase 2 wound trial is recruiting. No published study tests a 1% compounded cream, and no study measures longevity in people.
Each is listed below as it was run.

research.title: Skin after CO2 laser resurfacing, 2006 (USA)

facts.v: randomized to after-care skin products with or without GHK-Cu. Redness was scored by computer analysis and by blinded evaluators.
13 patients completed the study, all treated with a CO2 laser around the mouth
redness, wrinkles, overall skin appearance, and a validated patient questionnaire

research.found: No significant difference between groups in redness, wrinkles or overall skin quality on objective measures. Patients using GHK-Cu rated their improvement in skin quality higher on the questionnaire (P = .04).

src.label: Miller et al., Arch Facial Plast Surg, 2006

research.title: Crow's feet, one patient, 2016 (Korea)

facts.v: one patient, no control. A spray device (Jet-M) was used with a solution of copper-GHK, oligo-hyaluronic acid, rhodiola extract, tranexamic acid and beta-glucan.

research.found: Wrinkles around the treated eye looked smaller in photographs and biopsies showed more collagen. No adverse effect was reported. Because GHK-Cu was one of five ingredients used with a device, its own effect cannot be separated.

src.label: Byun et al., J Cosmet Laser Ther, 2016

research.text: Registered trials with no results yet

research.title: Small skin wounds, Phase 2

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled. Each person gets two small punch-biopsy wounds on the upper arm; one gets GHK-Cu gel, the other a plain gel.
how fast the wounds close, from photographs over 3 weeks, then scar quality
The same sponsor, Hudson Biotech, registered a TB-500 entry that describes itself as fictional: NCT07487363, first posted March 23, 2026.

research.found: Recruiting since February 2026. Estimated completion March 2028.

src.label: NCT07437586, ClinicalTrials.gov
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07487363

items.text: lab study of normal and radiation-damaged fibroblasts from head and neck surgery patients. GHK-Cu shortened their doubling time and raised early bFGF and VEGF output in the damaged cells.

src.label: Pollard et al., Arch Facial Plast Surg, 2005

items.text: 24 male rats with wounds in a poorly supplied skin flap, split into GHK-Cu gel, plain gel or no treatment, for 13 days. Wound area fell by 64.5% with GHK-Cu, 45.6% with plain gel and 28.2% with no treatment.

src.label: Canapp et al., Vet Surg, 2003

items.text: 18 rabbits with open wounds, split into GHK-Cu, zinc oxide or no treatment, for 21 days. Unhealed wound area was smaller with GHK-Cu than with no treatment on days 7, 14 and 21.

src.label: Cangul et al., Vet Dermatol, 2006

research.text: Animal and cell results have not been confirmed in people.

us.text: GHK-Cu is not an FDA-approved drug for any use. For compounding, FDA treats the injected form and the non-injected forms differently. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: none. FDA describes it only as a bulk substance nominated for compounding, and says there are limited data in humans to inform safety.

FDA, bulk drug substances nominated under section 503A (categories 1 to 3)

items.text: FDA placed “GHK-Cu (for injectable routes of administration)” in Category 2, substances that may present significant safety risks. It now appears on FDA’s list of Category 2 substances whose nominations were withdrawn. FDA says compounded injectable GHK-Cu may pose a risk of immune reactions because of aggregation and peptide-related impurities.

src.label: FDA, bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks (Category 2)

items.text: FDA removed GHK-Cu from Category 1 on April 22, 2026 after the nominations were withdrawn. On May 5, 2026 one nominator said it meant to withdraw only the injectable route, so FDA said “GHK-Cu (except for injectable routes of administration)” will be added back to Category 1 (under evaluation). FDA intends to consult its Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee before the end of February 2027.

items.text: under FDA’s interim policy, FDA does not intend to take action against a compounder using a Category 1 substance if the conditions in its guidance are met. That is enforcement discretion, not approval.

after.title: Sport
after.text: GHK-Cu is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or the 2027 list, which takes effect January 1, 2027. Class S0 bans any pharmacological substance with no current approval for human therapeutic use, and the 2027 list adds “peptides” to its examples. WADA’s 2027 notes say a peptide not named on the list may still be prohibited. Athletes should check with their anti-doping organization.

side.text: Human data on side effects are very limited. The few skin studies are small and short. FDA’s stated concerns are about injected GHK-Cu.

items.text: the 2006 laser-resurfacing study abstract does not report side effects. The 2016 single-patient report found no adverse effect.

items.text: Health Canada warns that unauthorized peptide drugs may contain too much, too little or none of the active ingredient, or contaminants, and lists risks including hormonal imbalance, blood sugar imbalance, liver or kidney damage and blood clots for this class of products.

unconfirmed: We could not confirm GHK-Cu's status as a cosmetic ingredient in a regulator's own record (the EU CosIng database could not be queried).
GHK-Cu facial studies often cited in reviews (for example from the late 1990s and early 2000s) were not found in PubMed or could not be opened, so they are not reported.
FDA's current Category 2 page does not show the date injectable GHK-Cu was first added to Category 2.
Status in the UK, EU and Australia was not checked against a regulator record.
DEA controlled-substance status was not checked.
surprises: The only randomized human skin study we found (13 people after laser resurfacing) showed no objective difference in redness, wrinkles or skin quality versus after-care without GHK-Cu; only patient-rated satisfaction differed.

FDA says there are limited human data on safety for injectable GHK-Cu and lists it as a possible immune-reaction risk, and Health Canada names injectable GHK-Cu among seized unauthorized drugs, although such peptides are promoted online for anti-aging.

Topical GHK-Cu was dropped from FDA's Category 1 on April 22, 2026 when nominations were withdrawn, then set to be restored after one nominator said it had meant to withdraw only the injectable route.
